proves.claim: requireChainDepth refuses CHAIN_TOO_DEEP when the longest --after chain through open items, itself counted, is deeper than 3, names the deepest chain and accepts depth 3.

cli.io-item-bar-depth.refuse-over-3.why: Without it, a regression where deep --after chains were filed would pass unnoticed and items would again stall behind their slowest link.

proves.claim: A merged, closed or unknown item is no link of the chain, a cycle ends where it repeats, and the edited item never counts as its own link.

cli.io-item-bar-depth.closed-items-and-c.why: Without it, a regression where closed items or a cycle inflated the measured depth would pass unnoticed and refuse valid filings.

proves.claim: The real add and edit commands refuse CHAIN_TOO_DEEP behind items.barRulesAtAdd, file nothing, and accept a chain of depth 3.

cli.io-item-bar-depth.add-refuses-deep.why: Without it, a regression where add or edit stopped calling requireChainDepth would pass unnoticed.
